source.title: Dimensionality-Driven Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Xingjun Ma; Yisen Wang; Michael E. Houle; Shuo Zhou; S. Erfani; Shu-Tao Xia; Sudanthi N. R. Wijewickrema; James Bailey

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure-only values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how training with partially corrupted labels changes held-out accuracy and representation dimensionality. It does not test memorization of fully random labels or the specific sharpness measure in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017)'s random-label result as prior work; that result is not this study's own. Figures 1–3 are described qualitatively, but their plotted values are figure-only. Table 1 reports test accuracy for cross-entropy and competing methods; rows below retain the cross-entropy results only.
record.test_reason: The study measures generalization under partial label corruption and its association with representation dimensionality. It does not measure the coexistence specified by V1: fitting fully random labels and generalizing on natural labels with the same architecture and training recipe. Random-label memorization is cited from Zhang et al.; none of V2–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors associate early dimensionality compression and later expansion with learning and overfitting under noisy labels, and propose monitoring LID and adapting the loss to suppress expansion and preserve test performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard SGD with momentum and cross-entropy for the baseline, but studies partial symmetric label corruption rather than fixed random labels and memorization capacity.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with label-noise proportion and dataset. Figure 1 also compares clean versus 40% noisy labels; the text describes different LID and accuracy trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-entropy test accuracy decreases as symmetric label corruption increases from 0% to 60% on all four datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard cross-entropy classifiers lose held-out accuracy as the proportion of incorrect training labels increases under the tested training budgets.

fits_no_version.finding: With 40% incorrect labels, LID initially decreases and then increases while test accuracy initially rises and then falls; clean-label training shows decreasing LID and increasing accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation dimensionality trajectories distinguish early pattern learning from later overfitting under partial label corruption.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 80, 2018
record.problems: The central trajectory evidence in Figure 1 is figure-only, with no numerical values in the text. The study does not test fully random labels or whether the networks fit those labels; its principal experiments use partial symmetric label corruption. Table 1 reports mean ± standard deviation over 5 repetitions.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 reports trajectories comparing D2L and competing methods for CIFAR-10 at 40% and 60% label noise, but the plotted values are figure-only and concern the proposed correction method. Figure 3 reports CSR comparisons as a plot without text values. Figure 4 is a t-SNE visualization. Figure 5 is a hyperparameter sensitivity plot. These results were not added as separate rows because they do not provide recoverable numeric measurements of a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed fully random labels, chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels, and coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V1 verdicts: clean-label accuracy alone does not test coexistence, and degradation under partial corruption does not limit V1. Table 1 training includes weight decay 10^-4; CIFAR training also uses augmentation. LID and CSR are different constructs from V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness. E2 describes D2L's comparative performance and should not be linked to V1 or presented as evidence for the cross-entropy rows.

versions.untested_parts: Tests standard SGD training with clean and partially corrupted labels, but not fitting fully random labels, near-perfect random-label training accuracy, or the same-architecture random-label versus natural-label comparison.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparison and local connectivity.
Batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 0% label noise on MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100
reader_labels.reason: Cross-entropy training yields the reported held-out accuracies under clean labels (R1, R5, R9, R13). This supports natural-label generalization in these settings, while the random-label memorization comparison is untested.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: 20%–60% symmetric label noise on the four reported datasets
reader_labels.reason: Cross-entropy test accuracy declines as the corrupted-label proportion rises; these conditions do not test fully random labels or perfect fitting (R2–R4, R6–R8, R10–R12, R14–R16).
